at kæle.explanation: "At kæle" means "to cuddle / pet". To name the animal or person you cuddle, add "med" (with) before it: "Hun kæler med hunden" (She cuddles the dog).

at kæmpe.explanation: "At kæmpe" means "to fight / struggle". To say a team fights hard in a match: "Holdet kæmper hårdt" (The team fights hard). To say something is difficult for you, add "med" (with): "Hun kæmper med lektierne" (She struggles with her homework). To say people argue, do not use "at kæmpe"; use "at skændes" (to argue): "Vi skændes om pengene" (We argue about the money).

at kæmpe for.explanation: "At kæmpe for" means "to fight for". To say you work hard for something you believe in: "Vi kæmper for retfærdighed" (We fight for justice). To say a team tries hard to win: "Holdet kæmper for sejren" (The team is fighting for the win).

at købe.explanation: "At købe" means "to buy". To say what you paid, add "for" (for) before the price: "Jeg købte den for hundrede kroner" (I bought it for a hundred kroner). To say who you buy something for, use "til" (to): "Jeg køber en gave til min mor" (I buy a gift for my mother).

at købe ind.explanation: "At købe ind" means "to buy groceries". To say you shop for a coming weekend: "Jeg køber ind til weekenden" (I am buying groceries for the weekend). To say you buy a single item, use "at købe" (to buy): "Jeg købte en bog" (I bought a book).

at køre.explanation: "At køre" means "to drive". To say you go by car: "Jeg kører i bil" (I go by car). To say a bus or train runs: "Bussen kører hver time" (The bus runs every hour). To say you go by bike, use "at cykle" (to cycle): "Jeg cykler på arbejde" (I cycle to work).

at køre fast.explanation: "At køre fast" means "to get stuck". To say a car cannot move on: "Bilen kørte fast i mudderet" (The car got stuck in the mud). To say a conversation stops moving forward: "Samtalen kørte fast" (The conversation got stuck).

at køre forbi.explanation: "At køre forbi" means "to drive past". To say you pass a shop in the car: "Vi kører forbi butikken" (We drive past the shop). To say you will visit someone briefly, the phrase means "to swing by": "Jeg kører forbi hos dig i aften" (I will swing by your place tonight).

at køre hjem.explanation: "At køre hjem" means "to drive home". To say you go home on foot, use "at gå hjem" (to walk home): "Jeg går hjem" (I am walking home). To say you are already at home, use "hjemme" (at home), not "hjem": "Jeg er hjemme" (I am at home).

en kaffeautomat.explanation: "En kaffeautomat" means "a coffee machine". It is built from "kaffe" (coffee) and "en automat" (a vending machine). To talk about the machine you brew coffee with at home, use "en kaffemaskine" (a coffee maker): "Jeg har en kaffemaskine derhjemme" (I have a coffee maker at home).

en kaffekande.explanation: "En kaffekande" means "a coffee pot". It is built from "kaffe" (coffee) and "en kande" (a pot). The same "kande" is in "en mælkekande" (a milk jug).

en kaffekop.explanation: "En kaffekop" means "a coffee cup". To name the coffee inside a cup, use "en kop kaffe" (a cup of coffee): "Jeg vil gerne have en kop kaffe" (I would like a cup of coffee).

en kaffemaskine.explanation: "En kaffemaskine" means "a coffee maker". It is built from "kaffe" (coffee) and "en maskine" (a machine). The same "maskine" is in "en vaskemaskine" (a washing machine).

en kaffepause.explanation: "En kaffepause" means "a coffee break". It is built from "kaffe" (coffee) and "en pause" (a break). To say you take a break without naming coffee, use "pause" alone: "Vi holder pause" (We take a break).

en kage.explanation: "En kage" means "a cake". To name the kind of cake, put the kind in front of "kage": "en fødselsdagskage" (a birthday cake) and "en chokoladekage" (a chocolate cake).

en kagedej.explanation: "En kagedej" means "a cake batter". It is built from "en kage" (a cake) and "en dej" (a dough). To ask to taste the batter: "Må jeg smage kagedejen?" (May I taste the cake batter?)

en kageform.explanation: "En kageform" means "a cake pan". It is built from "kage" (cake) and "en form" (a mold). "Form" also means "a shape": "en kage i form af et hjerte" (a cake in the shape of a heart).

en kagerulle.explanation: "En kagerulle" means "a rolling pin". It is built from "kage" (cake) and "en rulle" (a roll). To say you flatten dough with it: "Jeg ruller dejen ud med en kagerulle" (I roll out the dough with a rolling pin).

en kaj.explanation: "En kaj" means "a quay". To say you walk along the water by the boats: "Vi går en tur på kajen" (We take a walk on the quay).

en kakerlak.explanation: "En kakerlak" means "a cockroach". To say there are several, use the plural "kakerlakker": "Der er kakerlakker i køkkenet" (There are cockroaches in the kitchen).

en kalender.explanation: "En kalender" means "a calendar". To say you look up a date, use "i" (in): "Jeg kigger i kalenderen" (I am looking in the calendar).

en kalkun.explanation: "En kalkun" means "a turkey". When you talk about the meat, leave out "en": "Jeg vil have kalkun på min sandwich" (I want turkey on my sandwich). The country is a different word, "Tyrkiet" (Turkey): "Jeg rejser til Tyrkiet" (I am traveling to Turkey).

en kalorie.explanation: "En kalorie" means "a calorie". To say more than one, the plural is "kalorier": "Hvor mange kalorier er der i en pizza?" (How many calories are in a pizza?)

en kalv.explanation: "En kalv" means "a calf". To name the meat, use "kalvekød" (veal): "Jeg køber kalvekød til middag" (I am buying veal for dinner).

en kam.explanation: "En kam" means "a comb". To ask to borrow one: "Må jeg låne din kam?" (May I borrow your comb?)
